study.title: Acupuncture modulates the functional connectivity among the subcortical nucleus and fronto-parietal network in adolescents with internet addiction
study.study_design: Pre-post intervention study with healthy control comparison group; resting-state fMRI collected before and after acupuncture treatment in the IA group; HCs received one fMRI scan after enrollment with no treatment
study.population: Adolescents aged 18-30 years recruited from universities
study.inclusion_criteria: Each subject with IA met the clinical diagnostic criteria for IA (Beard & Wolf, 2001); only individuals with a score of more than 50 on the Internet Addiction Test (IAT) were included in the IA group; HCs did not meet the criteria for IA
study.exclusion_criteria: Subjects with substantial brain abnormalities or a history of substance dependence were excluded, as well as lactating or pregnant females

arms.dropouts: Three subjects with IA did not complete the acupuncture treatment due to schedule constraints

extraction_notes.note: No sham acupuncture or placebo control arm was included. The study compares acupuncture-treated IA subjects to untreated healthy controls only, limiting causal inference about acupuncture specificity.
Expectancy, credibility, and blinding success measures were not reported. The paper does not mention assessing these constructs.
Adverse events were not reported anywhere in the paper.
Ethics approval statement is not explicitly reported in the main text of the paper as provided.
Trial registration number was not reported.
Needle insertion depths per acupoint are reported in Table S1 (supplementary material), which was not provided in the PDF. Depth values per acupoint therefore cannot be extracted.

Figure S1 showing the acupoint locations and Table S1 showing needle insertion depths are referenced but not provided in the extracted PDF. Acupoint location details and individual depth values are unavailable.

The paper labels the seed region (MNI: −4, −31, −4) as both 'left posterior cingulate cortex (PCC)' in the Dosenbach/Yeo ROI atlas and as 'midbrain' in the Harvard-Oxford Atlas. These two labels are anatomically inconsistent. The paper acknowledges this discrepancy explicitly. Both labels preserved in extraction.

Specific node-to-node edge identities for the 1 increased SN intra-FC, 22 increased FPN intra-FC, and 15 increased SN-FPN inter-FC at baseline (Figure 2b, Figure 3a-d) are visible in figures but individual edge pair identities cannot all be reliably read from the OCR text. Only summary counts extracted.

Specific node-to-node edge identities for the 9 decreased FPN intra-FC and 31 decreased SN-FPN inter-FC after acupuncture (Figure 4b, Figure 5a-c) are visible in figures but individual edge pair identities cannot all be reliably read from the OCR text. Only summary counts extracted.

The sample size for post-treatment analyses is n=27 (3 dropouts from original n=30 IA group), but the paper's Table 1 shows n=27 for the IA group without explicitly confirming all 27 completed neuroimaging. The neuroimaging analyses are reported with n=27 based on the dropout description and Table 1.

The paper does not clearly specify whether Figure 2a p-values (P=0.063 for SN intra, P=0.025 for FPN intra, P=0.066 for SN-FPN inter) are from the average FC strength comparison between HCs and IA at baseline. These are inferred from the figure caption and surrounding text.

The paper does not clearly specify whether Figure 4a p-values (P=0.550 for SN intra, P=0.119 for FPN intra, P=0.033 for SN-FPN inter) are from paired t-tests comparing pre vs post in the IA group. These are inferred from the figure caption and surrounding text.

Deqi was described as an intended sensation but no quantitative instrument (e.g., MASS, Southampton Needle Sensation Questionnaire) was used to assess sensory responses. No numeric deqi scores are reported.

ROI coordinates for all 28 nodes (7 SN + 21 FPN) used in the FC network analysis are not listed in the main paper. They reference Dosenbach et al. (2010) and Yeo et al. (2011) atlases. Individual ROI coordinates are not extractable from this paper alone.

The multiple linear regression model R2=0.512 with n=27 may be subject to overfitting given the large number of candidate FC predictors entered into forward stepwise selection from the significant post-treatment FC changes. The paper notes no multicollinearity was detected but does not report cross-validation.
The paper does not report individual session-level IAT scores or any interim assessments between pre- and post-treatment timepoints.
